author: emcousin
body:
### Problem
We have dozens of instances of direct charge processor comparisons scattered across the codebase:
```ruby
if charge_processor_id == StripeChargeProcessor.charge_processor_id
```

This creates:
- Poor readability - verbose comparisons that don't express intent
- Maintenance burden - changes require updating every location
- Hard to expose to frontend - implementation details can't be easily serialized
- The last point is critical as we migrate admin to Inertia: we need clean, serializable methods to expose processor type logic to the frontend without leaking implementation details.

### Solution
Introduce `ChargeProcessable` concern with predicate methods:
```ruby
# Before ❌
if charge_processor_id == StripeChargeProcessor.charge_processor_id

# After ✅
if stripe_charge_processor?
```
- Clear intent - reads like natural language
- DRY - single source of truth
- Frontend-friendly - easy to serialize for Inertia props
- Tested - comprehensive test coverage

### Changes
- New `ChargeProcessable` concern with 3 predicate methods
- Refactored 23 comparisons across 13 files
- Included in `Purchase`, `MerchantAccount`, and `CreditCard` models

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The GbnfConverter was generating malformed GBNF grammar that caused parsing errors when used with LLama.cpp based backends. For example, given this simple class:

```csharp
public class BasicBitch
{
    public string Response { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public int Confidence { get; set; } = 0;
}
```

The converter was producing invalid GBNF:

```gbnf
root ::= "{" ws "Response" ws ":" ws root-Response ws "," ws root-Response ::= string
"Confidence" ws ":" ws root-Confidenceroot-Confidence ::= integer
 ws "}"
```

This resulted in the error:
```
parse: error parsing grammar: expecting newline or end at ::= string
"Confidence" ws ":" ws root-Confidenceroot-Confidence ::= integer
```

## Solution

Rewrote the GBNF generation to produce proper grammar compatible with LLama.cpp's parser:

### 1. Fixed Rule Separation
Each rule is now properly defined on its own line, preventing concatenation errors.

### 2. Updated Property Name Quoting
Changed from `"\"" "PropertyName" "\""` to the correct format `"\"PropertyName\""`.

### 3. Introduced Key-Value Pair Rules
Properties now use separate `-kv` rules that combine the property name with its value:
```gbnf
Response-kv ::= "\"Response\"" space ":" space Response
```

### 4. Improved Whitespace Handling
Replaced the simple `ws` rule with a more robust `space` rule that better handles formatting:
```gbnf
space ::= | " " | "\n"{1,2} [ \t]{0,20}
```

### 5. Enhanced Type Rules
- Added `space` suffix to all primitive type rules (integer, number, boolean)
- Introduced separate `char` rule with proper escape sequences
- Added `| null` support for nullable string types
- Split integer into `integer` and `integral-part` rules with proper bounds

## Result

The same BasicBitch class now generates valid GBNF:

```gbnf
root ::= "{" space Response-kv "," space Confidence-kv "}" space
Response ::= string | null
Response-kv ::= "\"Response\"" space ":" space Response
Confidence-kv ::= "\"Confidence\"" space ":" space integer

# Utility rules
char ::= [^"\\\x7F\x00-\x1F] | [\\] (["\\bfnrt] | "u" [0-9a-fA-F]{4})
integer ::= ("-"? integral-part) space
integral-part ::= [0] | [1-9] [0-9]{0,15}
null ::= "null" space
number ::= ("-"? integral-part) ("." [0-9]+)? ([eE] [-+]? [0-9]+)? space
space ::= | " " | "\n"{1,2} [ \t]{0,20}
string ::= "\"" char* "\"" space
```

This format is fully compatible with LLama.cpp based backends and matches the expected GBNF grammar specification.

## Testing

All existing tests have been updated to reflect the new format and pass successfully. The generated GBNF has been validated to ensure:
- No malformed line breaks
- Each rule is properly defined on its own line
- All rules follow the correct syntax
- Format matches LLama.cpp expectations

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Okay, so we recently worked on tools / GbnfConverter but it's not working yet.
> 
> For testing purpose: I made a BasicBitch class:
> 
>     public class BasicBitch
>     {
>         public string Response { get; set; } = string.Empty;
>         public int Confidence { get; set; } = 0;
>     }
> 
> This gave me the following GBNF
> 
> root ::= "{" ws "Response" ws ":" ws root-Response ws "," ws root-Response ::= string
> "Confidence" ws ":" ws root-Confidenceroot-Confidence ::= integer
>  ws "}"
> 
> # Utility rules
> ws ::= [ \t\n]*
> string ::= "\"" ([^"\\] | "\\" ["\\/bfnrt] | "\\u" [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F] [0-9a-fA-F])* "\""
> number ::= "-"? ("0" | [1-9] [0-9]*) ("." [0-9]+)? ([eE] [-+]? [0-9]+)?
> integer ::= "-"? ("0" | [1-9] [0-9]*)
> 
> 
> But when run against LLama.cpp based backends, i get the following error:
> 
> parse: error parsing grammar: expecting newline or end at ::= string
> "Confidence" ws ":" ws root-Confidenceroot-Confidence ::= integer
>  ws "}"
> 
> A correct GBNF for this file would be:
> 
> Confidence-kv ::= "\"Confidence\"" space ":" space integer
> Response ::= string | null
> Response-kv ::= "\"Response\"" space ":" space Response
> char ::= [^"\\\x7F\x00-\x1F] | [\\] (["\\bfnrt] | "u" [0-9a-fA-F]{4})
> integer ::= ("-"? integral-part) space
> integral-part ::= [0] | [1-9] [0-9]{0,15}
> null ::= "null" space
> root ::= "{" space Response-kv "," space Confidence-kv "}" space
> space ::= | " " | "\n"{1,2} [ \t]{0,20}
> string ::= "\"" char* "\"" space
> 
> Can you help?

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses all four known limitations identified in the README and implements three high-value additional features for the Library Manager application.

## Problems Solved

### 1. Thread Safety (Critical)
The `DatabaseManager` class was not thread-safe, which could lead to race conditions when accessed from both UI and background threads (e.g., during file scanning and analysis).

**Solution**: Added `juce::CriticalSection` mutex protection to all database operations. Every method that accesses the SQLite database now uses `const juce::ScopedLock lock(dbMutex)` to ensure exclusive access. This includes all CRUD operations for Tracks, VirtualFolders, FolderTrackLink, Jobs, and the new CuePoints table.

### 2. Chromaprint Library Detection
While conditional compilation was in place, there was no runtime method to check if the Chromaprint library was available.

**Solution**: Added a static `isAvailable()` method to `AcoustIDFingerprinter` that returns compile-time configuration status, allowing the application to dynamically adapt UI and functionality based on library availability.

### 3. Playlist Editing - Drag and Drop
Users had no way to add tracks to playlists through the UI.

**Solution**: Implemented full drag-and-drop functionality:
- `LibraryTableComponent` now provides `getDragSourceDescription()` to package selected track IDs
- `PlaylistTreeComponent::PlaylistItem` accepts drops via `isInterestedInDragSource()` and `itemDropped()`
- Automatic duplicate detection prevents adding the same track twice
- Visual feedback updates the playlist's verification status immediately

### 4. Advanced Cue Point Support
Only basic tempo markers were exported to Rekordbox XML, lacking professional DJ cue point features.

**Solution**: Created comprehensive cue point system:
- New `CuePoints` database table with fields for position, name, type, hot cue number, and color
- Full CRUD operations: `addCuePoint()`, `updateCuePoint()`, `deleteCuePoint()`, `getCuePoint()`, `getCuePointsForTrack()`, `deleteAllCuePointsForTrack()`
- Enhanced Rekordbox export to include `POSITION_MARK` elements for Memory Cues and Hot Cues
- Maintains backward compatibility with basic `TEMPO` markers when no cue points exist

## Additional Features Implemented

### 5. Batch Metadata Editing
Users can now edit metadata for multiple tracks simultaneously through a modal dialog interface. The `BatchMetadataEditor` component allows selective editing of Artist, Album, Genre, BPM, and Key fields with checkbox controls to choose which fields to update. Accessible via right-click context menu on selected tracks in the library table.

### 6. Smart Playlists with Auto-Filtering
Implemented dynamic playlists that automatically populate based on metadata criteria:
- Extended `VirtualFolder` structure with `isSmartPlaylist` and `smartCriteria` fields
- Criteria format: `"artist:value;genre:value;bpmMin:120;bpmMax:140"`
- `evaluateSmartPlaylist()` method dynamically queries matching tracks at runtime
- **Security**: Uses parameterized queries with `sqlite3_bind_text()`/`sqlite3_bind_int()` to prevent SQL injection
- **Validation**: Numeric values validated before use in queries
- Automatic database migration adds new columns to existing installations

## Technical Improvements

### Security
- Fixed SQL injection vulnerabilities in smart playlist evaluation
- All user input properly escaped and validated
- Parameterized queries throughout

### Database Schema
- Automatic migration system detects and adds missing columns
- New `CuePoints` table with foreign key relationships
- Smart playlist columns added to `VirtualFolders` table
- Full backward compatibility maintained

### Code Quality
- Zero build errors with GCC 13.3.0
- Comprehensive error logging with `sqlite3_errmsg()`
- RAII patterns throughout (no memory leaks)
- Consistent with existing codebase style

## Testing

All existing tests pass:
- `TestDatabaseManager.cpp`
- `TestRekordboxExport.cpp`
- `TestLibraryComponents.cpp`

Manual testing recommended for:
- Drag-and-drop between library and playlists
- Batch metadata editor dialog
- Smart playlist evaluation
- Cross-platform builds (Windows, macOS)
- Rekordbox XML import validation

## Migration

The application includes automatic database migration logic that:
1. Detects existing databases without new columns
2. Adds columns with appropriate defaults (`is_smart_playlist=0`, etc.)
3. Preserves all existing data
4. Logs migration success/failure

No manual migration steps required for users.

## Documentation

Added comprehensive `IMPLEMENTATION_FEATURES.md` with:
- Detailed description of all changes
- Usage examples for new features
- Security considerations
- Performance characteristics
- Future enhancement suggestions

---

**Ready for**: Production deployment after platform-specific testing and Rekordbox import validation.

### useS3Upload훅 내부에서 mutateAsync사용 이유
- 업로드 완료 후 업로드된 최종 URL을 호출 측에서 바로 써야 했기 때문.
- mutate는 콜백 기반이어서 호출부에서 값을 다루기 번거로운 반면, mutateAsync는 Promise를 반환하므로 await로 직접 결과({ uploadedUrl })를 받는 것 가능
- 그래서 훅 외부에서는 await uploadFile(file, imageType)처럼 동기식 흐름으로 결과를 간결하게 사용 가능

### useS3Upload훅에서 “POST + PUT”을 하나의 mutationFn에 넣은 이유

- Presigned URL 발급과 업로드는 실질적으로 분리 불가능한 한 트랜잭션처럼 동작
- 둘을 분리하면 Presigned URL만 남거나 만료되는 경계 상태가 생길 수 있고, 에러/중복처리/재시도 정책이 분산되어 복잡도 증가
- 한 mutation에서 순차 실행하면 원자성, 에러 처리 일관성, 재시도 정책을 한 곳에서 관리 가능

body:
## Summary

This PR rewrites the hoganpad application from Vue 2 with vanilla JavaScript to a modern stack using **Vite + React + TypeScript**. The rewrite maintains 100% feature parity with the original implementation while adding type safety and a modern development experience.

## Changes Made

### Infrastructure
- **Added `.gitignore`**: Node.js gitignore file to exclude `node_modules`, `dist`, logs, and other build artifacts
- **Vite Setup**: Modern build tool with hot module replacement (HMR)
- **TypeScript**: Full type safety across the entire codebase
- **React 19**: Latest React with hooks-based architecture
- **Package Scripts**: `dev`, `build`, `lint`, and `preview` commands

### Code Structure

**Type Definitions** (`src/types.ts`)
- `Item` - Represents text and box items on the canvas
- `Selection` - Tracks the current selection rectangle
- `SelectionComputed` - Computed selection bounds

**Utilities** (`src/utils.ts`)
- Migrated from `utils.js` to TypeScript
- Grid size constants and helper functions
- Selection computation logic

**React Components**
- `HoganGrid.tsx` - Renders the grid background lines
- `HoganSelection.tsx` - Displays the selection rectangle
- `HoganItemText.tsx` - Renders text items with heading support
- `HoganItemBox.tsx` - Renders box items with text alignment
- `App.tsx` - Main application with all state management and event handling

### Features Preserved

All functionality from the original Vue 2 application has been maintained:

- ✅ **Grid-based canvas** - A4-sized (700x1020px) grid paper with 20px cells
- ✅ **Text and box creation** - Double-click or type to create items
- ✅ **Keyboard navigation** - Arrow keys, Enter, Delete, F2
- ✅ **Mouse interaction** - Click to select, drag to multi-select, drag tab to move items
- ✅ **LocalStorage persistence** - Items are automatically saved and restored
- ✅ **Markdown headings** - Support for `#`, `##`, `###` for different heading sizes
- ✅ **Text anchoring** - Use `:` prefix/suffix for left/right text alignment in boxes
- ✅ **Print styling** - Grid lines and selections hidden when printing
- ✅ **Item dragging** - Drag items to reposition them with visual preview

## Technical Highlights

**Migration from Vue 2 to React**
```javascript
// Before (Vue 2)
Vue.component("hogan-grid", {
  props: ["width", "height"],
  template: `<g>...</g>`,
  computed: { ... }
});

// After (React + TypeScript)
export default function HoganGrid({ width, height }: HoganGridProps) {
  const vlines = range(width / 20).map(i => i * 20 + 0.5);
  return <g>...</g>;
}
```

**Type Safety**
All data structures now have proper TypeScript types, preventing runtime errors and improving developer experience with IntelliSense.

## Screenshots

**Initial state with example data:**
![Initial hoganpad](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8722a36-7d8f-4a36-8ca7-1172bda967f3)

**After adding new text showing keyboard navigation:**
![Adding text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81686904-77a0-4335-a985-b7281f22e5d9)

## Development

```bash
# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start development server with HMR
npm run dev

# Build for production
npm run build

# Run linter
npm run lint

# Preview production build
npm run preview
```

## Migration Notes

- The original `svg.js` and `utils.js` files have been removed and replaced with TypeScript equivalents
- The `canvas/` directory remains unchanged (appears to be an alternative implementation)
- All CSS styles have been preserved and migrated to `src/App.css` and `src/index.css`
- The application maintains the same visual appearance and user experience

author: h-huang
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #165664

We currently use `_add_send_recv()` to inject the `send()` and `recv()` calls into the schedule IR:

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/7d87d7052ef40fc802d8340c6a56ce3b7beb8407/torch/distributed/pipelining/schedules.py#L1152-L1153

We make an underlying assumption that calling `recv()` only schedules the operation and does not block the communication stream until it is `wait()`-ed on. This seems to not be the case and we see that the `recv` blocks the `send` on the communication stream which causes a cascading bubble since rank 0 cannot execute all of its sends for stage 0, unless it has received the data for stage 8.

This changes the IR so that during the warmup phase, recv is set after the forwards.

Before:
```
[0UNSHARD, 8UNSHARD, 0F0, 0SEND_F0, 8RECV_F0, 0F1, 0SEND_F1, 8RECV_F1, 0F2, 0SEND_F2, 8RECV_F2, 0F3, 0SEND_F3, 8RECV_F3, ...]
```

Now:
```
[0UNSHARD, 8UNSHARD, 0F0, 0SEND_F0, 0F1, 0SEND_F1, 0F2, 0SEND_F2, 0F3, 0SEND_F3, ...]
```

I believe there are alternative ways to fix this:

- Use separate streams for `send` and `recv` calls. This also requires different PP groups for those different streams since they can't share the same communicator
- Use one-sided NVSHMEM APIs put/get

I think using `put`/`get` instead is promising and should be explored.

cc @awgu @wanchaol @fegin @fduwjj @wz337 @wconstab @d4l3k @pragupta @msaroufim @dcci

body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR adds a new serverless function template for a URL shortener using the Python runtime. This function allows users to:
1.  Create a unique, short ID for any given long URL.
2.  Handle HTTP redirections from the short URL to the original long URL.

The implementation uses the `nanoid` library for generating short IDs and the official `appwrite-server-sdk` for database interactions, making it a robust and practical example for the templates collection.

## Test Plan

The function has been tested locally by following these steps:

**1. Appwrite Setup:**
* Created a new database in an Appwrite project.
* Created a new collection within the database.
* Added a single **String Attribute** to the collection with the key `original_url`, a size of `2048`, and marked it as **required**.
* Saved the Database ID and Collection ID for the environment variables.

**2. Function Deployment:**
* Navigated to the `python/url-shortener/` directory.
* Created a compressed `code.tar.gz` file of the source code.
* Created a new function in the Appwrite console and uploaded the `code.tar.gz` file.
* Added the following environment variables in the function's settings:
    * `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`
    * `APPWRITE_API_KEY`
    * `APPWRITE_PROJECT`
    * `DATABASE_ID` (from step 1)
    * `COLLECTION_ID` (from step 1)
* Deployed the function.

**3. Execution and Verification:**

* **Test Case 1: Creating a Short URL**
    * Executed the function with the following JSON payload:
        ```json
        {
          "url": "[https://appwrite.io/](https://appwrite.io/)"
        }
        ```
    * **Result:** The function executed successfully and returned a JSON response containing the `short_url`, confirming the document was created in the database.

* **Test Case 2: Redirecting to the Original URL**
    * Copied the document ID (the short ID) from the result of the previous test.
    * Executed the function again with the following JSON payload:
        ```json
        {
          "short_id": "[COPIED_SHORT_ID_HERE]"
        }
        ```
    * **Result:** The function correctly issued a `301 redirect` to the original URL (`https://appwrite.io/`), verifying the lookup and redirect logic.

## Related PRs and Issues

None.

Yes.

author: jcrist
body:
This is a general cleanup or our linear regression implementation.

A few notable changes:

- I added a new `algorithm="auto"` option and made it the default. The user-facing behavior is the same, but having it default to `"auto"` better indicates that the algorithm is chosen automatically rather than switching from `eig` to `svd` when needed.
- We now only warn when falling back to `svd` if the user explictly set `algorithm` to something other than `auto`. In the auto case the fallback happens without a warning. This matches the behavior in `Ridge` as well.
- This fixes a bug where input arrays were being mutated, even if `copy_X=True`. This was due to a misunderstanding in what cases a copy was needed, and also what arrays may be mutated. I've added a more thorough test and cleaned up the copy handling to better reflect the requirements. We now only copy input arrays at most once, and do so only when needed. We also ensure that none of `X`, `y`, or `sample_weight` are accidentally mutated by the solvers.

Part of #7317.

body:
## Summary

Fixed TS2345 type mismatch errors across 17 files where CacheEngine constructor parameters were in the wrong order or cache.set() received incorrect parameter types.

### Root Cause
- CacheEngine constructor signature: `constructor(dbPath?: string, maxMemoryItems: number = 1000)`
- Code was incorrectly calling: `new CacheEngine(100, path)` (wrong order)
- Should be: `new CacheEngine(path, 100)` (correct order)

- CacheEngine.set() signature: `set(key: string, value: string, originalSize: number, compressedSize: number)`
- Code was incorrectly calling: `cache.set(key, value, ttl, "utf-8")` (wrong parameters)
- Should be: `cache.set(key, value, size, size)` (correct parameters)

author: codyshoffner
body:
## Description

- Swap away from bitnami images for the valkey & valkey sentinel deployments.
- The Valkey Sentinel docker image has been removed, but valkey sentinel can be deployed from the standard valkey image.

- I would love feedback on this draft, primarily as it pertains to the `values/values.yaml`. I do not love the new implementation. There is not an upstream helm chart that supports sentinel, except for the bitnami one that is currently being used. 
In the `values/values.yaml`, I had to figure out how the bitnami startup scripts would create a sentinel.conf, then recreate it myself. I am open to suggestions on how this could better be implemented. 

- Unfortunately, I had to continue using bitnamilegacy for the redis-exporter image, as bitnami has a hardcoded bash wrapper for the exporter, which only get's enabled whenever you enable sentinel. There are no upstream redis-exporter images that support a bash terminal.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview
Updated the README.md to accurately reflect the significant progress made on the Cassanova Casino project. The previous README showed many features as "to-do" items in the roadmap, but these features have been fully implemented and are now live in the application.

## Changes Made

### 🎯 Key Features Section Reorganization
Restructured the Key Features section into four distinct categories for better clarity:
- **Frontend Experience** - Added documentation for Game Detail Pages, User Dashboard, and enhanced Promotional System
- **Authentication & Security** - New section highlighting the complete auth system with login/register pages, protected routes, and session management
- **Financial Management** - New section documenting multi-payment deposits, secure withdrawals, transaction history, and balance tracking
- **Casino Features** - Updated to reflect backend-ready implementations

### 📸 Enhanced Demo Section
Expanded the Demo section to showcase all major application areas:
- Authentication Pages (login/registration with validation)
- User Dashboard (account overview, balance, VIP tracking, transactions)
- Game Pages (lobby and individual game detail pages)
- Financial Pages (deposit and withdrawal with multiple payment methods)
- Promotion Pages (listing and individual promotion details)

### 🌐 New Frontend Routes Documentation
Added a dedicated section documenting the application's routing structure:
- **Public Routes**: Homepage, login, register, dynamic game pages, dynamic promotion pages
- **Protected Routes**: Dashboard, deposit, and withdraw pages requiring authentication

### 🏗️ Updated Project Structure
Updated the file structure diagram to show all new directories and files:
- Authentication pages (`login/`, `register/`)
- User areas (`dashboard/`, `deposit/`, `withdraw/`)
- Dynamic routes (`games/[slug]/`, `promotions/[slug]/`)
- Utility libraries (`lib/api.ts`, `lib/auth-context.tsx`)
- Type definitions (`types/`)

### 📋 Roadmap Reorganization
Restructured the roadmap to celebrate completed work and prioritize future features:

**✅ Completed Features** (new section):
- Phase 1: Core Pages - 5 major page implementations complete
- Phase 2: User Experience - 6 UX enhancements complete

**🚀 Upcoming Features** (reorganized):
- Short Term: Email verification, password reset, 2FA, etc.
- Medium Term: Payment provider integration, admin dashboard, live chat
- Long Term: Game provider integration, live dealer, mobile apps

### 📚 Documentation Updates
- Added reference to `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` for detailed feature documentation
- Updated project structure to match current state
- All technology versions verified as accurate

## Impact
This update provides an accurate representation of the project's current state, properly documenting the 11 completed features across authentication, user management, game pages, financial transactions, and promotions. The README now serves as a reliable reference for developers and stakeholders to understand what's been built and what's planned.

## Related Documentation
- See `IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` for detailed technical documentation of the implemented features
- All completed features have been tested and are production-ready with zero build errors or warnings

author: mihalicyn
body:
During our work on arm64 GCS (aka shadow stack) we found (thanks to `sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=0`) that the way how we restore x86 shadow stack is not quite correct. I need to dive into details to explain why.

During shadow stack restore we abusing so called "premapped" VMAs. It is purely CRIU concept, and we use it to ensure proper CoW restoration for anonymous VMAs. Idea is simple, early on restore we prepare VMAs and fill them with a data from page images. Then, when we start forking processes they can naturally inherit those VMAs and CoW flags will be properly set in the kernel. Of course, this has nothing to do with shadow stack that's why I said "abusing" instead of using. :)

So, basically, for shadow stack we were "premapping" (and, important, NON-shadow stack, but regular anon) VMA with the size `original_shadow_stack_size + 1 page`. And intention was simple, we were putting original shadow stack contents to it and one extra page was basically a place holder for a temporary shadow stack we need for restorer PIE to function properly. Then, once we reach `vma_remap(vma_entry, args->uffd)` loops, we were just skipping those premapped VMAs because at that time we still need them as we restore shadow stack *after* that loop, but this is the problem. We can't just skip mappings in that loops (https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/blob/c14c2ae842ebe6c15e635e5ed6ff2b65cdd229d8/criu/pie/restorer.c#L1821 and https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/blob/c14c2ae842ebe6c15e635e5ed6ff2b65cdd229d8/criu/pie/restorer.c#L1845) because the entire algorithm only functions if VMAs are remapped in the proper order.

Igor (@svilenkov) noticed, that something fails there on his testing system all the time. This was a hint for us to recheck x86 shadow stack too, but it wasn't failing. Missing piece of puzzle was `sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=0` which Igor was using on his testing VM. Enabling this on my x86 machine immediately made x86 shadow stack to fail too. Like this:
```
# ./test/zdtm.py run -t zdtm/static/pthread00 -f h
userns is supported
=== Run 1/1 ================ zdtm/static/pthread00
======================== Run zdtm/static/pthread00 in h ========================
Start test
./pthread00 --pidfile=pthread00.pid --outfile=pthread00.out
Run criu dump
Run criu restore
=[log]=> dump/zdtm/static/pthread00/62/1/restore.log
------------------------ grep Error ------------------------
b'(00.008718) pie: 62: Remap 0x7ffff495f000->0x7ffff59fe000 len 0x1000'
b'(00.008726) pie: 62: Remap 0x7ffff415f000->0x7ffff51fe000 len 0x800000'
b'(00.008744) pie: 62: Remap 0x7ffff415e000->0x7ffff51fd000 len 0x1000'
b'(00.008753) pie: 62: Remap 0x7fffef97e000->0x7ffff0021000 len 0x3fdf000'
b'(00.008758) pie: 62: Error (criu/pie/restorer.c:1153): Unable to map a guard page 0x7ffff3fff000 (0x7ffff7fba000)'
b'(00.008768) pie: 62: Error (criu/pie/restorer.c:2329): Restorer fail 62'
b'(00.008785) Error (criu/cr-restore.c:2324): Restoring FAILED.'
b'(00.008928) Error (criu/cr-restore.c:1258): 62 exited, status=1'
------------------------ ERROR OVER ------------------------
############### Test zdtm/static/pthread00 FAIL at CRIU restore ################
```
or like this:
```
# ./test/zdtm.py run -t zdtm/static/pthread00 -f h
userns is supported
=== Run 1/1 ================ zdtm/static/pthread00
======================== Run zdtm/static/pthread00 in h ========================
Start test
./pthread00 --pidfile=pthread00.pid --outfile=pthread00.out
Run criu dump
Run criu restore
=[log]=> dump/zdtm/static/pthread00/62/1/restore.log
------------------------ grep Error ------------------------
b'(00.008507) pie: 62: Restoring scheduler params 0.0.0'
b'(00.008517) pie: 62: rseq: rseq_abi_pointer = 0x7ffff7f9e060 signature = 0x53053053'
b'(00.008520) pie: 62: Using clone3 to restore the process'
b'(00.008544) pie: 62: Using clone3 to restore the process'
b'(00.008551) pie: 63: Error (criu/arch/x86/include/asm/shstk.h:89): Failed to map shadow stack at 0x7ffff6200000: -17'
b'(00.008554) pie: 63: Error (criu/pie/restorer.c:830): Restorer abnormal termination for 62'
b'(00.008583) Error (criu/cr-restore.c:2324): Restoring FAILED.'
b'(00.008702) Error (criu/cr-restore.c:1258): 62 exited, status=1'
------------------------ ERROR OVER ------------------------
############### Test zdtm/static/pthread00 FAIL at CRIU restore ################
```

The idea of the right fix belongs to Andrei. We have to restore shadow stack VMA right in vma remap loop. Once it is our turn, we do:
1. create shadow stack vma in a random place
2. fill it with data from a premapped VMA
3. unmap premapped VMA
4. mark shadow stack VMA address as a "premapped" one
5. let `vma_remap` function to do its job to properly `mremap` it to the final destination 

Fixes: https://github.com/checkpoint-restore/criu/pull/2306

author: konard
body:
## Описание изменений

Этот PR реализует правильный алгоритм глобальной интерполяции B-сплайнов для функции `ConvertOnCurvePointsToControlPointsArray`, которая вычисляет контрольные точки сплайна таким образом, чтобы результирующая кривая проходила точно через заданные точки.

### 📋 Связанная задача
Fixes #204

### 🔧 Реализованные изменения

1. **Исправлена функция базиса BasisFunction** (`uzccommand_spline.pas:87-162`)
   - Реализован корректный алгоритм рекурсии Кокса-де Бура с использованием треугольной таблицы
   - Добавлена правильная обработка граничных случаев и деления на ноль
   - Улучшена численная стабильность

2. **Заменен решатель системы уравнений** (`uzccommand_spline.pas:179-236`)
   - Удален упрощенный трехдиагональный решатель (Thomas algorithm)
   - Реализован метод Гаусса с частичным выбором ведущего элемента
   - Поддержка решения полной системы линейных уравнений

3. **Переработана функция ConvertOnCurvePointsToControlPointsArray** (`uzccommand_spline.pas:238-338`)
   - Реализована правильная глобальная интерполяция B-сплайнов
   - Построение матрицы коэффициентов N из значений базисных функций
   - Решение системы N * P = D для нахождения контрольных точек P
   - Удалены неправильные упрощения и аппроксимации

### 📐 Математическая основа

Алгоритм решает задачу глобальной интерполяции B-сплайнами:
- Для n заданных точек D₀, D₁, ..., Dₙ₋₁
- Находим n контрольных точек P₀, P₁, ..., Pₙ₋₁
- Такие что B-сплайн кривая C(u) проходит через все заданные точки

Метод:
1. Параметризация по длине хорды (chord length parameterization)
2. Генерация узлового вектора (clamped uniform knot vector)
3. Построение матрицы N[i][j] = BasisFunction(j, degree, params[i])
4. Решение системы уравнений для каждой координаты (x, y, z)

### ✅ Результат

Теперь сплайн корректно проходит через все указанные пользователем точки, как показано на скриншотах в issue #204:
- Сплайн интерполирует (проходит через) заданные точки
- Контрольные точки вычисляются автоматически
- Кривая имеет гладкую форму с правильной кривизной

### 🧪 Тестирование

Реализованный алгоритм:
- Корректно обрабатывает граничные случаи (2 точки, линейные сплайны)
- Работает для различных степеней сплайна (особенно degree=3, кубические)
- Обеспечивает численную стабильность благодаря частичному выбору главного элемента

body:
This PR implements a simple Node.js script that exposes a function called `addify` which adds all provided number values together.

## Implementation

The `addify` function is implemented in `index.js` and uses:
- ES6 rest parameters (`...numbers`) to accept any number of arguments
- `Array.reduce()` to sum all values, starting from an initial value of 0
- Returns 0 when no arguments are provided

```javascript
const addify = require('./index');

author: abhi-markan
body:
# Introduction :pencil2:

When files are changed on a container, due to multi-stage build `docker restart` does not works and often requires building docker containers again. This PR introduced hot-reloading using `nodemon`.

This PR utilise existing `NODE_ENV` variable for ascertaining nodemon execution, as it is only executed for non-production enviornments (when `NODE_ENV` is not set to `production`).

## Resolution :heavy_check_mark:

* Introduced `start:dev` service to execute `nodemon` with `--config` CLI argument.
* Refactored `Dockerfile` to add `nodemon.json` and `start.sh` files to the container's root directory.
* Updated `docker-compose.yml` with `server` as mount directories and removed `entrypoint`.

## Miscellaneous :heavy_plus_sign:

* Dependencies updates.

#### What is the purpose of this pull request?

This PR updates TypeScript types for suggestion objects so that the `fix` property is required.

This prevents creating suggestions without a fix, which would otherwise cause the runtime error:
```
TypeError: context.report() called with a suggest option without a fix function.
```

It also broadens the type of `data` from `Record<string, string>` → `Record<string, unknown>` because ESLint message interpolation can accept any value that can be stringified.

#### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

- Made `fix` required in `SuggestedEditBase`.
- Changed `data` type to `Record<string, unknown>` for compatibility with ESLint message interpolation.
- Added tests for `data` to ensure various types are allowed.
- Added `@ts-expect-error` in test where `fix: null` is used.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive audit visualization system for technical audits (Auditorias IMCA) with a card-based UI, color-coded status badges, and formatted date display.

## What's New

### Database Layer
Extended the `auditorias_imca` table with 6 new fields to support detailed audit tracking:
- `navio` - Ship name being audited
- `data` - Date of the audit
- `norma` - Standard/norm used (e.g., IMCA, ISO 9001)
- `resultado` - Result status with CHECK constraint: "Conforme", "Não Conforme", or "Observação"
- `item_auditado` - Specific item or area audited
- `comentarios` - Additional comments and observations

Added performance indexes on `data`, `navio`, and `resultado` fields for efficient querying.

### API Endpoint
Created `GET /api/auditorias/list` endpoint that:
- Fetches all audits from the database with proper authentication
- Returns audits ordered by date (newest first)
- Includes comprehensive error handling
- Integrates with Supabase Row Level Security (RLS)

### UI Component
Built the `ListaAuditoriasIMCA` React component featuring:

**Visual Design:**
- Card-based layout with shadow effects and hover transitions
- Ship emoji (🚢) for vessel identification
- Clipboard emoji (📋) for the section title
- Responsive spacing and typography

**Status Indicators:**
- 🟢 Green badge (`bg-green-100 text-green-800`) for "Conforme" (compliant)
- 🔴 Red badge (`bg-red-100 text-red-800`) for "Não Conforme" (non-compliant)
- 🟡 Yellow badge (`bg-yellow-100 text-yellow-800`) for "Observação" (observation)

**User Experience:**
- Loading state with spinner message while fetching data
- Empty state when no audits are registered
- Date formatting using `date-fns` in dd/MM/yyyy format
- Conditional rendering of comments field

### Admin Integration

*  change the check to service account creation in `ExpectApplied` from checking when the object is a pod to checking if its a namespace
* This avoids having to change existing unit tests to mock service account creation API calls when calling `ExpectApplied` for pods. 

For context: the change to add the service account creation to `ExpectApplied` was done fairly recently (last week) in this PR: https://github.com/awslabs/operatorpkg/pull/188. We discovered that pulling in this new version broke existing unit tests that used mock APIs. By splitting this up, we now keep existing functionality for `ExpectApplied` and introduce `ExpectNamespaceApplied`

## Summary

This PR implements automated code translation workflows for the LinksPlatform repository, addressing issue #168 which requested a GitHub extension/app for automatic language translation.

### 🚀 Implemented Solutions

#### 1. **Code Translation Workflow** (`.github/workflows/code-translation.yml`)
- **Purpose:** Bidirectional C# ↔ VB.NET code conversion
- **Technology:** [ICSharpCode.CodeConverter](https://github.com/icsharpcode/CodeConverter) (Roslyn-based)
- **Features:**
  - ✅ High-accuracy translation using Roslyn compiler
  - ✅ Support for entire projects and directories
  - ✅ Manual workflow dispatch with configurable parameters
  - ✅ Automatic pull request creation with translated code
  - ✅ Translation artifacts saved for 30 days

**How to use:**
1. Navigate to Actions → Code Translation
2. Click "Run workflow"
3. Select source/target languages (csharp or vb)
4. Specify the path to translate (default: Platform)
5. Choose whether to create a PR automatically

#### 2. **AI-Powered Code Translation Workflow** (`.github/workflows/ai-code-translation.yml`)
- **Purpose:** Multi-language code translation using AI
- **Technology:** OpenAI GPT-4 API
- **Supported Languages:** Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C#, C++, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, VB.NET
- **Features:**
  - ✅ Intelligent translation preserving logic and style
  - ✅ Comments and documentation translation
  - ✅ Automatic PR creation with AI-generated code
  - ✅ Optional integration (requires OPENAI_API_KEY secret)

**How to use:**
1. Add `OPENAI_API_KEY` to repository secrets (Settings → Secrets)
2. Navigate to Actions → AI-Powered Code Translation
3. Click "Run workflow"
4. Specify the source file and target language
5. Enable "Use OpenAI" option

#### 3. **Documentation** (`.github/CODE_TRANSLATION.md`)
- Comprehensive guide for both workflows
- Setup instructions for AI-powered translation
- Alternative tools and resources
- Best practices and important notes

### 🔗 Related Issues
- Fixes #168 - GitHub extension/app for automatic language translation
- Related to #119 - Translate Everything
- Related to #488 - Programming languages translation

### 📝 Implementation Details

**Workflow 1: C#/VB.NET Translation**
- Uses the official ICSharpCode.CodeConverter CLI tool
- Installed via `dotnet tool install --global ICSharpCode.CodeConverter.CLI`
- Validates that source and target languages are different
- Creates a new branch for each translation: `code-translation/{source}-to-{target}-{run_number}`
- Labels PRs with `automated` and `code-translation`

**Workflow 2: AI Translation**
- Uses Python with OpenAI API client
- GPT-4 model for best translation quality (temperature=0.1 for consistency)
- Automatically extracts code from markdown responses
- Determines appropriate file extensions for each language
- Includes detailed PR descriptions with warnings about AI-generated code

### ✅ Testing

- [x] YAML syntax validated using Python's yaml module
- [x] Workflow structure follows GitHub Actions best practices
- [x] Both workflows use `workflow_dispatch` for manual triggering
- [x] Proper error handling and validation
- [x] Clear user instructions and feedback

### ⚠️ Important Notes

1. **For C#/VB.NET translation:** Works out of the box, no setup required
2. **For AI translation:** Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret and OpenAI API credits
3. **All translations should be reviewed:** Automated translation may require manual adjustments
4. **Test translated code:** Verify functionality, dependencies, and edge cases before merging

### 🎯 Benefits

- **Accessibility:** Developers can work in their preferred .NET language
- **Code Examples:** Easy generation of code examples in multiple languages
- **Legacy Migration:** Facilitate migration from VB.NET to C#
- **Multi-language Support:** Extend codebase to other programming languages
- **Automated Process:** No manual copy-paste to online converters

### 📚 Documentation

Full documentation is available in [`.github/CODE_TRANSLATION.md`](.github/CODE_TRANSLATION.md), including:
- Detailed usage instructions for both workflows
- Setup guide for OpenAI integration
- Alternative translation tools
- Contributing guidelines
- Best practices for reviewing translated code

author: giwahassan722
body:
A decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) for community-driven museum curation using Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain.

## 🏛️ Overview

MuseDAO enables communities to collectively curate digital museum collections through democratic governance and blockchain technology. The system allows anyone to submit artifacts, vote on their inclusion, and participate in the governance of digital museum collections.

## ✨ Key Features

- **Community-Driven Curation**: Democratic voting system for artifact inclusion
- **Digital Artifact Management**: Secure registration and metadata storage for museum pieces
- **Decentralized Governance**: Token-based voting for collection management
- **Collection Categories**: Multiple museum categories (Art, History, Science, etc.)
- **Curator Reputation**: Track and reward active community curators
- **Transparent Operations**: All curation decisions recorded on-chain
- **Exhibition Management**: Create and manage themed exhibitions

## 🏗️ Architecture

The system consists of two main smart contracts:

### 1. Collection Manager Contract (`collection-manager.clar`)
- Manages digital artifacts and their metadata
- Handles collection categorization and organization
- Tracks artifact provenance and ownership
- Manages exhibition creation and artifact assignment
- Controls access permissions for different user roles

### 2. Curator Governance Contract (`curator-governance.clar`)
- Implements DAO voting mechanisms for curation decisions
- Manages curator registration and reputation systems
- Handles proposal creation and voting processes
- Distributes governance tokens to active participants
- Tracks voting history and curator contributions

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites
- Clarinet CLI installed
- Stacks wallet for testing
- Basic understanding of Clarity smart contracts

### Installation

1. Clone or download the project
2. Navigate to the project directory:
   ```bash
   cd MuseDAO
   ```

3. Check contract syntax:
   ```bash
   clarinet check
   ```

4. Run tests:
   ```bash
   clarinet test
   ```

## 📋 Contract Functions

### Collection Manager Functions
- `register-artifact`: Submit a new digital artifact to the museum
- `update-artifact-metadata`: Update artifact information
- `create-collection`: Create a new museum collection category
- `add-artifact-to-collection`: Assign artifacts to specific collections
- `create-exhibition`: Create themed exhibitions
- `get-artifact-info`: Retrieve artifact details and metadata
- `get-collection-info`: View collection information

### Curator Governance Functions
- `register-curator`: Join the DAO as a curator
- `create-proposal`: Propose new artifacts or governance changes
- `vote-on-proposal`: Cast votes on pending proposals
- `execute-proposal`: Execute approved proposals
- `claim-curator-rewards`: Claim governance tokens for participation
- `get-proposal-info`: View proposal details and voting status
- `get-curator-info`: Check curator reputation and voting history

## 🗂️ Collection Categories

### Supported Categories
1. **Fine Arts**: Paintings, sculptures, digital art
2. **Historical Artifacts**: Documents, photographs, memorabilia
3. **Natural History**: Specimens, fossils, geological samples
4. **Science & Technology**: Inventions, instruments, innovations
5. **Cultural Heritage**: Traditional crafts, ceremonial objects
6. **Literature**: Manuscripts, books, written works
7. **Photography**: Historic and artistic photographs
8. **Archaeology**: Ancient artifacts, archaeological finds

## 🗳️ Governance System

### Voting Process
1. **Proposal Creation**: Curators propose new artifacts or changes
2. **Community Review**: 7-day review period for proposals
3. **Voting Period**: 5-day voting window for all registered curators
4. **Execution**: Approved proposals are automatically executed
5. **Rewards Distribution**: Active voters receive governance tokens

### Curator Levels
- **Novice Curator**: 0-10 successful votes
- **Associate Curator**: 11-50 successful votes  
- **Senior Curator**: 51-100 successful votes
- **Master Curator**: 100+ successful votes
- **Honorary Curator**: Special recognition for outstanding contributions

## 💰 Token Economics

### Governance Tokens
- **Voting Power**: 1 token = 1 vote
- **Earning Methods**: Successful proposals, active voting, quality submissions
- **Token Supply**: Dynamic supply based on community activity
- **Staking Rewards**: Additional tokens for long-term participation

### Curator Incentives
- Successful artifact submissions earn tokens
- Consistent voting participation rewarded
- Quality control bonuses for accurate curation
- Exhibition creation rewards

## 🔒 Security Features

- **Multi-signature Requirements**: Major decisions require consensus
- **Time-locked Proposals**: Mandatory review periods prevent rushed decisions
- **Reputation-based Voting**: Experienced curators have more influence
- **Audit Trail**: Complete history of all curation decisions
- **Access Controls**: Role-based permissions for different functions

## 📊 Use Cases

1. **Digital Art Museums**: Community-curated online art galleries
2. **Historical Archives**: Decentralized preservation of historical documents
3. **Scientific Collections**: Collaborative scientific specimen databases
4. **Cultural Preservation**: Community-driven cultural heritage projects
5. **Educational Resources**: Curated educational content collections
6. **Virtual Exhibitions**: Themed digital exhibitions and displays

## 🛠️ Technical Specifications

### Smart Contract Features
- **Gas Optimization**: Efficient contract execution
- **Scalability**: Support for large collections
- **Interoperability**: Compatible with NFT standards
- **Upgradability**: Governance-controlled contract improvements
- **Data Integrity**: Tamper-proof artifact records

### Data Storage
- **On-chain Metadata**: Essential artifact information stored on blockchain
- **IPFS Integration**: Large files stored on distributed storage
- **Provenance Tracking**: Complete ownership and transfer history
- **Backup Systems**: Redundant storage for critical data

## 🌟 Advanced Features

### Exhibition System
- Create themed virtual exhibitions
- Curate collections around specific topics
- Schedule timed exhibitions with start/end dates
- Track exhibition visitor metrics
- Award badges for exhibition participation

### Reputation System
- Track curator accuracy and participation
- Reward consistent quality contributions
- Implement peer review mechanisms
- Create curator leaderboards
- Recognition badges and achievements

## 🤝 Community Governance

### DAO Structure
- **Proposal Types**: Artifact submissions, policy changes, budget allocation
- **Voting Mechanisms**: Simple majority, supermajority, quadratic voting
- **Quorum Requirements**: Minimum participation thresholds
- **Veto Powers**: Emergency safeguards for malicious proposals
- **Treasury Management**: Community-controlled funding allocation

### Participation Rewards
- **Active Voting**: Tokens for consistent participation
- **Quality Submissions**: Bonuses for approved artifacts
- **Community Building**: Rewards for onboarding new curators
- **Technical Contributions**: Incentives for platform improvements

## 📈 Roadmap

### Phase 1: Foundation (Current)
- Basic artifact management
- Simple voting mechanisms
- Core collection categories
- Curator registration system

### Phase 2: Enhancement
- Advanced exhibition features
- Reputation system implementation
- Mobile app development
- API for external integrations

### Phase 3: Expansion  
- Cross-chain compatibility
- AI-powered curation assistance
- Virtual reality museum experiences
- Institutional partnerships

## 🧪 Testing

The project includes comprehensive test suites covering:
- Artifact registration and management
- Voting mechanism accuracy
- Governance token distribution
- Access control systems
- Edge cases and error handling

Run tests with:
```bash
clarinet test
``

# Add test for tool calling node stacktrace in rejected event

## Summary
Added test coverage to verify that when a tool in a ToolCallingNode throws an error, the resulting rejected event includes a stacktrace field. This ensures that debugging information is properly propagated when tools fail during workflow execution.

**Changes:**
- Added `error_tool()` helper function that always raises a `ValueError` 
- Added `test_tool_calling_node__tool_error_includes_stacktrace()` test that:
  - Creates a ToolCallingNode with a tool that errors
  - Verifies node rejection events are emitted
  - Asserts that the stacktrace field exists and contains error details

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] **Verify stacktrace content is sufficient for debugging** - Check that the stacktrace includes enough information to debug real tool errors (file names, line numbers, etc.), not just that it exists and contains the error message
- [ ] **Confirm error wrapping behavior** - The test expects "NodeException" in the stacktrace (not "ValueError") because tool errors are wrapped. Verify this is the intended behavior and that the original exception information is still accessible
- [ ] **Validate mock accuracy** - Ensure the test's mock setup (LLM returning a function call that then errors) accurately simulates how tool errors occur in production

### Test Plan
```bash
cd vellum-python-sdks
poetry run pytest tests/workflows/basic_tool_calling_node/tests/test_workflow.py::test_tool_calling_node__tool_error_includes_stacktrace -xvs
```

### Notes
- Test was added to the existing `basic_tool_calling_node` test suite since it tests ToolCallingNode behavior
- Helper function `error_tool()` was added to `get_current_weather.py` for simplicity (keeping test tools together)

This pull request introduces a comprehensive Dialog (modal) UI component suite, including its implementation, styling, integration, localization, and tests. The Dialog components are modular, customizable, and follow best practices for composition and accessibility. Additionally, supporting styles and i18n strings are added, along with a playground page and thorough unit tests.

**Dialog Component Suite Implementation:**

* Added a full set of Dialog components (`Dialog.vue`, `DialogTrigger.vue`, `DialogContent.vue`, `DialogHeader.vue`, `DialogFooter.vue`, `DialogTitle.vue`, `DialogDescription.vue`, `DialogOverlay.vue`, `DialogClose.vue`) using `reka-ui` primitives and compositional slots for flexible usage. Each component supports custom classes and props for extensibility. It also adds a comprehensive README to guide contributors and updates the `.dockerignore` for improved cleanliness. Deprecated or redundant actions are removed, streamlining the CI/CD pipeline and making it easier to maintain and extend.

**Key changes:**

### New Composite Actions for CI/CD

* Added `.github/actions/build-portfolio/action.yml` to build the Astro portfolio app, with options for type checking, artifact upload, and build statistics.
* Added `.github/actions/build-api/action.yml` to validate and build the Cloudflare Workers API, including Wrangler config validation and type generation.
* Added `.github/actions/lint/action.yml` for Biome linting, TypeScript, Astro checks, and accessibility checks, with status outputs and summary generation.
* Added `.github/actions/test-playwright/action.yml` for Playwright E2E testing with browser caching, artifact uploads, and flexible browser/mode selection.
* Enhanced `.github/actions/setup/action.yml` for monorepo setup, supporting configurable Node.js versions, pnpm caching, and verification steps.

### Documentation & Onboarding

* Added `.github/README.md` with a quick start guide, detailed action/workflow documentation, usage examples, and CI/CD best practices.

### Cleanup & Removal of Deprecated Actions

* Removed `.github/actions/install/action.yml` in favor of the new, more flexible setup action.
* Removed `.github/actions/setup-token/action.yml` as part of action consolidation and simplification.

### CI/CD Hygiene

* Updated `.dockerignore` to include `*.tmp`, reducing unnecessary files in Docker contexts.

---

These changes modernize the workflow, improve CI speed and reliability, and make the repository easier to contribute to and maintain.
